## A confession

I first mentioned `pins` to you in 2020.

Then again in 2022.

Almost made a presentation about it in March.

. . .


Today we are really using it.


## The scenario

You have spent three weeks cleaning a 2 GB fish dataset.

You need it in three places:

- your laptop
- the iDiv RStudio server
- EVE cluster

. . .

What do you do?

## What we usually do

```
local_computer/projects/
├── paper_1/data/fish_FINAL.csv           # 2.1 GB
├── paper_2/data/fish_FINAL_v2.csv        # 2.2 GB
└── paper_3/data/fish_cleaned_NEW.csv     # 2.0 GB
```
```
Rstudio_server/work/
├── paper_2/data/fish_FINAL_v2.csv           # 2.0 GB
└── paper_3/data/fish_cleaned_NEW_v2.csv     # 2.3 GB
```

. . .

```r
data <- read.csv("/Users/yourname/projects/paper_1/data/fish_FINAL.csv")
```

Various copies. Five paths. Two systems. Many chances to use the wrong version.

## {background-color="#000643"}

::: {.black-quote}
"An absolute path is a burden<br>passed on yourself"
:::

## What `pins` gives you

- **One** canonical copy of your data, with a stable name
- Works with any R object: data frames, models, lists, vectors
- Automatic **versioning** — no more `_FINAL_v2`
- Reads the latest version by default; older versions are always there

## Two concepts

**pin** — any R object, saved to a named location

**board** — the location itself (folder, server, cloud storage)

. . .

```r
board <- board_local()

pin_write(board = board, x = my_data, name = "fish_survey")
pin_read(board  = board, name = "fish_survey")
```

## Different locations for boards

| Location | Good for | Command |
|---|---|---|
| inside working directory | personal, single machine, versioning data | `board_local()` |
| in your dropbox | reusing data between projects | `board_folder("C:/dropbox/invasive_fish_project")` |
| shared H: drive | rstudio server, team sharing | `board_folder("H:/synthesis/pins_Alban")` |
| one script | local ↔ EVE | `board_folder("~/pins")` + `rsync` |

## Before & after

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Before**

```r
dt <- read.csv(
  paste0(
    "/Users/yourname/projects/",
    "paper_1/data/",
    "fish_FINAL_v3.csv"
  )
)
# Error on EVE.
# Error for your colleague.
# Which version is this again?
```
:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**After**

```r
board <- pins::board_folder(
  path = GROUP_PINS_PATH
)

dt <- pins::pin_read(
  board = board,
  name  = "fish_survey"
)
# Works on your laptop.
# Works on EVE.
# Always the latest version.
```
:::

::::

## Versioning

Every `pin_write()` creates a new version automatically.

```r
pins::pin_versions(board = board, name = "fish_survey")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   version                created             hash
#>   <chr>                  <dttm>              <chr>
#> 1 20240315T091233Z-8e4f… 2024-03-15 09:12    8e4f1…
#> 2 20240820T142211Z-c3a1… 2024-08-20 14:22    c3a10…
#> 3 20250104T083445Z-f2b9… 2025-01-04 08:34    f2b91…
```

`pin_read()` loads the latest by default. Pass `version =` to pin a specific one.

## The H: drive and EVE

For **Rstudio server or team sharing**: H: is the same files — just a different path by OS.

```r
# Windows
board <- pins::board_folder(path = "H:\synthesis\pins_Alban")
# Mac
board <- pins::board_folder(path = "/Volumes/synthesis/pins_Alban")
```

. . .

We will come back to this with `.Rprofile`

## The H: drive and EVE
For **EVE**: `pins` stores everything in a plain folder — sync it.

```bash
# macOS / Linux
rsync -avz ~/work/pins/ frontend1.eve.ufz.de:~/pins

# Windows — PowerShell (OpenSSH built-in since Windows 10)
scp -r .\work\pins\ frontend1.eve.ufz.de:~/pins
```

```r
# identical code on both machines
board <- pins::board_folder(path = GROUP_PINS_PATH)
```

## {background-color="#000643"}

::: {.black-single}
One board.<br>Any machine.
:::

## Setup in 3 lines {.center}

```r
board <- pins::board_local()

pins::pin_write(board = board, x = my_data, name = "my_dataset")
```

. . .

Reading from any project:

```r
board <- pins::board_local()

pins::pin_read(board = board, name = "my_dataset")
```

## Create a board and write a pin {auto-animate=true}

```{r}
#| label: demo-board
#| eval: true
#| message: false
board <- pins::board_local()
```

. . .

```{r}
#| label: demo-write-1
#| eval: true
fish_2024 <- data.frame(
  species   = c("Esox lucius", "Perca fluviatilis", "Abramis brama"),
  abundance = c(12L, 45L, 8L),
  site      = rep(x = "Lake Müggelsee", times = 3L)
)

pins::pin_write(
  board       = board,
  x           = fish_2024,
  name        = "fish_survey",
  description = "Annual fish survey, Lake Müggelsee, 2024"
)
```

## Read it back — from any project {auto-animate=true}

```{r}
#| label: demo-read
#| eval: true
pins::pin_read(board = board, name = "fish_survey")
```

## Update the data, write a new version

```{r}
#| label: demo-write-2
#| eval: true
fish_2025 <- rbind(
  fish_2024,
  data.frame(
    species   = "Rutilus rutilus",
    abundance = 31L,
    site      = "Lake Müggelsee"
  )
)

pins::pin_write(
  board       = board,
  x           = fish_2025,
  name        = "fish_survey",
  description = "Annual fish survey, Lake Müggelsee, 2025 update"
)
```
##  Update the data, write a new version

```{r}
#| label: demo-versions
#| eval: true
pins::pin_versions(board = board, name = "fish_survey")
```

## When `pins` doesn't help

- Files that must stay in their original format (`.xlsx` with macros, raw rasters)
- Data too large to load into memory
- Data that is never shared or reused across projects, not even with paper reviewers

. . .

For those cases: keep the file on H:, document the path in your README,
and version the cleaning script in git.

## Getting started today

1. `install.packages("pins")`
2. Create a local board — write one pin from an existing project
3. If it sticks → move to H: or ~/volume/groups/synthesis for the team

. . .

The only way to know if it helps is to try it in a real project.

## Don't wanna?

Maybe these could be useful:

 - `rsync` in your .Rprofile so that everytime you open R, data is synchronised between your computer and EVE
 -  use `..` in path to go one level up. If your data is in a different folder in the same parent folder: `read.csv("../external_data_folder/my_data.csv`
